summary: AI agents and open benchmarks for finding manufacturable semiconductor materials.
editor_note: Open benchmark data makes this materials-search product more inspectable than most AI-for-science claims. Its agents evaluated 526 thermal-interface candidates across 30–100M-token runs, while the team publishes both the dataset and benchmark. Unlike a black-box lab-service pitch, researchers can interrogate the search process and failure cases. The real test is whether more than one of 500-plus candidates can reach a plausible synthesis route.
investors: Lightspeed Venture Partners,Peak XV Partners,Y Combinator

sources.label: Discovered Materials official research and benchmark page

product_evidence.claim: Discovered Materials publishes a 526-material dataset and a benchmark for evaluating AI agents that search for thermally conductive dielectric materials.
The official research page documents agent runs spanning 30–100M tokens and makes the material records downloadable instead of exposing only a promotional result.

market_context.primary_user: Semiconductor materials researchers and engineering teams evaluating candidate dielectrics for thermal-interface applications.
market_context.differentiation: The company pairs agentic search with a public dataset and benchmark, making the discovery process and failure modes more inspectable than a closed research service.
market_context.why_now: The August 2026 Seed follows the release of a concrete benchmark and dataset at a time when AI-for-science claims need reproducible evidence.

risks.claim: Whether the search process can repeatedly turn ranked candidates into plausible synthesis routes can be tested as the company publishes follow-on lab validation.
risks.basis: The official research page says only one of more than 500 evaluated candidates had a plausible synthesis route.
